changes.text: Moved to the new CMF-CD platform, as a common successor to the X-Trail T31 and the Rogue S35.
changes.quote: Based on an all-new CMF-CD platform shared with the Nissan Qashqai and Renault Koleos, the vehicle is a common successor for the second generation X-Trail and the Rogue that is offered in North America.

changes.text: The rugged, squared-off lines of the previous X-Trail were dropped for a new design.
changes.quote: In place of the rugged, squared off lines of the previous generation, new X-Trail has a premium and dynamic appearance.

changes.text: A largely plastic tailgate saves 7 kg, part of weight savings made although the vehicle has a larger surface area.
changes.quote: This has been achieved on all counts by reducing weight wherever possible, even though new X-Trail has a larger surface area than the previous model. The tailgate, for example, is largely plastic, saving seven kilograms.

changes.text: A longer wheelbase gives more second-row knee room.
changes.quote: Middle row seat comfort has been improved thanks to extra knee room generated by the longer wheelbase

changes.text: Three-row, seven-seat versions were added alongside the two-row, five-seat versions.
changes.quote: In addition to two-row five-passenger grades, three-row seven-passenger grades are newly added.

changes.text: Optional three-row, seven-passenger seating was offered in the Rogue for the first time.
changes.quote: For the first time, Rogue will offer optional 3-row/7-passenger seating, thanks to its improved interior packaging efficiency.

changes.text: Active Ride Control and Active Engine Brake were introduced.
changes.quote: Advanced technologies, including world's first Active Ride Control and Active Engine Brake, and Cornering Stability Assist, are adopted in all grades

salesStart.quote: Im September 2017 wurde der X-Trail einer Modellpflege unterzogen.

changes.text: Larger grille, wider chrome surround and square fog lamps; revised rear bumper and LED tail lights.
changes.quote: Die Frontpartie besitzt einen größeren Grill. Außerdem ist die Chromspange nun breiter und markanter. Die Nebelscheinwerfer sind ab sofort eckig. Im Heckbereich gibt es einen geänderten Stoßfänger und Rückleuchten in LED-Technik.

changes.text: Boot volume rose by 15 litres to 565 litres.
changes.quote: Der Kofferraum hat nun ein Volumen von 565 Liter (+15 Liter).

changes.text: The Rogue was facelifted for the 2017 model year with restyled headlights and tail lights and standard LED daytime running lights.
changes.quote: The Rogue was facelifted for the 2017 model year, with restyled headlights and tail lights, and LED daytime running lights standard on all trim levels.

notes: First generation sold as both X-Trail and (in the US and Canada) Rogue. Specifications differ by market: the US Rogue used the 2.5 QR25DE (170 hp) and, for 2017–2019, a hybrid; the European X-Trail used 1.3/1.6 petrol and 1.6/1.7/2.0 diesel engines; the Japanese X-Trail used the 2.0 MR20DD (and later a hybrid). Records are kept separate by market.
Ordinal 3 is the X-Trail count; for the Rogue line this is the second generation.

Production end 2022 is from Wikipedia's X-Trail infobox; the Rogue T32 ended with the 2020 model year, and Dongfeng Nissan continued building the T32 in China as the X-Trail Honor (2021–2023) and X-Trail Classic (2023–).
Rogue third-row seating was dropped for the 2018 model year (Wikipedia: 'For the 2018 model year, Nissan decided to drop the third row option').

Dimensions: only Wikipedia infobox figures were found (Rogue article: 182.7 in long; X-Trail article gives ranges of 4,640–4,690 mm, so only the wheelbase is recorded for the X-Trail). No manufacturer dimension sheet for T32 was readable.

Seating: 5- and 7-seat versions are documented in words by Nissan ("two-row five-passenger grades, three-row seven-passenger grades"), but no quotable digits were found, so the seating field is left empty.

The 2017 facelift dates differ: European facelift September 2017 (German Wikipedia), 2017 model year in North America (Rogue), October 2016 per English Wikipedia's X-Trail article. English Wikipedia's X-Trail facelift paragraph appears to reuse North American Rogue text (S/SV/SL trims, Divide-N-Hide) and was not used for X-Trail facts.

The European powertrain records come from German Wikipedia's specification table, where the columns are 1.3 DIG-T, 1.6 DIG-T, 1.6 dCi, 1.7 dCi and 2.0 dCi; values were matched to engines by column order and should be double-checked.
Commons also has 'Category:Nissan Rogue (T32)' (90 files) for the North American model.

notes: The Rogue (US/Canada, built in Smyrna and Kyushu) appeared first (revealed June 2020, 2021 model year); the X-Trail followed in China in April 2021, Australia in May 2022, Japan in July 2022 and Europe in 2022. The generation-level reveal date is the Rogue's; the X-Trail was unveiled at Auto Shanghai on 19 April 2021 (Wikipedia).

Engines differ by market and must not be mixed: US Rogue 2.5 PR25DD (2021) then 1.5 KR15DDT VC-Turbo (2022–; Canada kept the 2.5 on the base model until the 2024 refresh); Japan e-POWER only; Europe e-POWER (2WD 150 kW / e-4ORCE 157 kW) and a 1.5 VC-T mild hybrid (120 kW); Australia, Middle East and Mexico a 2.5-litre petrol; China a 1.5 VC-Turbo.
The 2027 Rogue press kit (still T33) lists overall length 184.4 in and height 67.9 in, versus 183.0 in and 66.5 in for the 2021 model year.
Platform naming: Nissan Ireland says Alliance CMF-C; Wikipedia says CMF-CD.
The T33 Rogue continued for the 2027 model year (2027 Nissan Rogue press kit, KR15DDT engine) alongside the T34-based 2027 Rogue Hybrid.

Facelift dating is unclear: English Wikipedia says a facelifted X-Trail was launched on 21 August 2025 (Nismo and Rock Creek added; market not stated, apparently Japan), while German Wikipedia says a revised version was presented in March 2026. Commons 'Category:Nissan X-Trail (2025)' is used for the facelift; reviewers should confirm it matches r3.
The Japanese e-POWER output figures were not found in a readable Nissan source and are omitted.
Commons also has 'Category:Nissan Rogue (T33)' (63 files) for the North American model.

changes.text: First Rogue offered with the e-POWER series hybrid drivetrain.
changes.quote: It is the first Rogue to be available with Nissan's e-Power series hybrid drivetrain, as well as being the first e-Power model to go on sale in the US.

changes.text: A thinner inner liftgate trim adds about 1.75 in of cargo length compared with the outgoing Rogue.
changes.quote: The inner liftgate trim is thinner than in the outgoing Rogue, so there's about 1.75 inches of additional length available in the trunk.

changes.text: Climate-controlled seats became available for the first time in a Rogue.
changes.quote: For the first time in Rogue, climate-controlled seats are available.

changes.text: The driver-assistance system gained a new front radar, a front camera with a 20% wider field of view and updated software, compared with the 2026 Rogue.
changes.quote: A new front radar sensor, a new front camera with a 20% wider field of view and updated software help the system operate more naturally across a wider range of driving situations, compared to the 2026 Rogue.

notes: Only the US Rogue Hybrid is documented here from Nissan's 2027 Rogue Hybrid press kit; X-Trail (non-US) specifications for T34 were not found in a readable source.
Reveal date conflict: English Wikipedia's X-Trail article says 14 April 2026, its Rogue article says April 13, 2026; recorded only to the month.
No production start date was found; Nissan says the Rogue Hybrid reaches US dealers in fall 2026 (SR AWD first, full range early 2027).
Cargo behind the second row conflicts within the Nissan press kit: 31.1 cu ft in the text and 34.4 cu ft in the specification table; neither is recorded.

The T34 is sold in the US alongside the carried-over T33 Rogue (petrol, 2027 model year). A separate Rogue Plug-in Hybrid (2026) is a rebadged Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV and is not part of this generation.
